title: Polynomial-time bounded iteration
statement: Let $f$ and $s$ be polynomial-time computable functions on Boolean words, and let $N$ be a natural-valued function whose unary encoding is polynomial-time computable. Suppose there is a natural number $K$ such that for every input $x$ and every $j\le N(x)$, the $j$-fold iterate of $f$ applied to $s(x)$ has length at most $K\bigl(|s(x)|+N(x)+1\bigr)^2$. Then the function mapping $x$ to the $N(x)$-fold iterate of $f$ applied to $s(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: the unary encoding of $N(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
there is $K\in\mathbb{N}$ bounding every iterate length for all $j\le N(x)$ by $K(|s(x)|+N(x)+1)^2$
replaced: Let $f$, an initial-word producer $s$, and a unary count producer $N$ be polynomial-time computable, and suppose every iterate of $f$ up to $N$ of the input has length at most $K((|s| + N + 1))^2$ in the produced values. Then the function sending an input $x$ to the $N(x)$-fold iterate of $f$ at $s(x)$ is polynomial-time computable; each iteration is one clean call inside the real unary repetition host.
